Dongshan remarked, "Having traveled together for twenty years, have you come to speak such words? Is this really your level of practice? The Master asked, "And what about you, Elder?"
Dong said, "It is like the principle of the great earth bursting into flames. One day he asked Dongshan, "There is nowhere that the reach of wisdom and consciousness does not traverse;
I beg the Master for a single word regarding the direct shortcut. Dongshan said, "How can you, my senior master, claim to have attained any merit?
Because of this, the teacher suddenly awakened, and his subsequent utterances were no longer ordinary.
One day, when West Garden (Xiyuan) the Abbot was bathing by himself, a monk asked, "Why does the Abbot not employ a śrāmaṇera or a novice?
Xiyuan clapped his hands three times. The monk reported this to Caoshan, who said, "In one sense, it is the same as clapping or patting the hands."
Among these, Xiyuan’s “strange” case and Juzhi’s “one-finger Zen” are both instances where the point of realization was not perfectly grasped.
A monk asked, "When Xiyuan clapped his hands, was that not the business of slaves and servants?
Xiyuan said, "Yes. The monk asked, "Is there anything further above this? Xiyuan said, "There is. The monk asked, "What is the matter further above? Xiyuan—
Deshan said, "This slave, this servant!
Tiantong commented, "He recognizes rank and knows the noble from the lowly; Xiyuan was a master who distinguished jade from stone and discerned gold from brass.
Caoshan did not appear in the world [to challenge him]. Although this monk understands how to polish and refine, he still remains among the servants."
The child and the servant girl lie fallen by his side. Do you know? "Leisurely and drenched, neither is harmed"—yet they are still guests outside the curtain of the night-bright moon.
When Chan Master Shanhui of Jia Shan was visited by Lu Pu, he did not prostrate; instead, he stood facing him with his hands folded in greeting.
The Master said, "A rooster nesting in a phoenix’s nest—these are not of the same kind. Begone! Yunluo said, "I have come from afar to seek your teaching;

I pray that you will grant me an interview. The Master said, "Before my eyes there is no *śrāmaṇera*; here there is no old monk. Yunluo then gave a shout. The Master said, "Wait, wait! Do not be so hasty and reckless.
The clouds and moon are the same, yet the streams and mountains differ. [You must] cut off all people in the world..."
"The tongue is not non-existent; how could one make a person without a tongue understand speech? As Luo stood there reflecting, the Master struck him.
From this, Luo came to take the Master's teachings to heart. Xinghua spoke on his behalf: "Simply know how to become a Buddha; do not worry about sentient beings."
Luopu fell into a state of solitary peril; thus, he did not know the path for turning himself around. Xinghua spoke on his behalf, saying, "Just know how to become a Buddha;
do not worry about sentient beings. This would have been exactly right to strike him with a staff and drive him out. Did he not know that Jia Shan was one who "kills the Buddha upon meeting him"?
Tiantong’s verse says: Shaking its head and wagging its tail, the crimson-scaled fish; Thoroughly without reliance, it knows how to turn the body. Severing the tongue, it possesses skill;
Dragging back the nostrils, it wondrously penetrates the spirit. Beyond the curtain at night, wind and moon are as bright as day;
Before the withered tree on the cliff, flowers and plants bloom forever in spring. The tongueless person—the tongueless person—is truly so.
"Causing one to personally grasp the single phrase; walking alone within the world, clearly and fully aware. Let the whole world rejoice as it pleases. He ascended the hall and said:
"The enlightened do not cross the threshold; the hollow does not nest in the tree. The eyes do not look back toward other positions; the feet do not tread [upon them]."
Within his state, the six gates are never closed; on the four crossroads, no tracks remain. His study does not pause at midday;

his mind does not establish the profound. For a thousand kalpas, the eye does not borrow from the base of the tongue; for ten thousand kalpas, the tongue does not look back upon the clarity within the eye.
With such a lofty faculty, there is no need for sharp edges. When things reach this point, what matter is there? "The thread on the tip of the pole is for you to play with"—do not violate it.
The clear waves have a meaning that is naturally distinct.
Danxia’s verse says: "The moon sinks into the blue sea, yet the dragon does not hide; Mist locks the Azure Tuo, yet the phoenix remains unaware.
Beyond the kalpas stands the dense, shadowless tree; It casts its shade, possessing branches that have not yet sprouted."
A monk arrived for an audience. The Master asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The monk replied, "Dongshan. The Master asked, "What words or phrases did Dongshan speak?
The monk said, "The Master said, 'I have three paths to receive people. The Master asked, "What are these three paths? The monk said:
The Bird’s Path, the Mysterious Road, and the Outstretched Hand. The Master said, "Do these three paths truly exist? The monk replied, "Yes.
The Master said, "Holding a begging bowl across a thousand li—how sad for the practitioner beneath the forest trees!"
Huangshan asked Wheel about his realization. The Master said, "Where have you come from? Wheel said, "From Min.
The Master said, "Do you recognize this old monk? Wheel said, "Does the Master recognize this student? The Master said, "Not so. First, pay me the price for my straw sandals;
then, this old monk will return to you the price of the rice from Luling. Wheel said, "In that case, I do not recognize [you]."
"Preceptor, I do not yet know: what is the price of rice in Luling? The Master said, "A true lion cub; he knows how to roar the lion’s roar. Danxia’s verse says:
"Father and son meet, their eyes grow twice as bright; they walk with ease amidst the clusters of spiritual sprouts. This...
If one were to say that the son of the Golden-Haired One has already seasoned the great soup with salt and plum;
when the monk questioned Chan Master Caoshan Benji, "What is it like when facing a guest during the five ranks? the Master said, "Which rank are you asking about right now?
The monk replied, "I have come from the partial rank; I request that the Master receive me within the correct rank. The Master said:
He did not acknowledge him. The monk asked, "Why do you not acknowledge me? The Master said, "I fear you would fall into a state of partiality.
The Master then asked the monk, "As for this non-acknowledgment, is it directed toward the guest or not? The monk replied, "It has already been directed toward the guest. The Master said:
"So it is, so it is. Danxia’s verse says: The jade hare in the moon conceives in the night; The golden crow in the sun broods on its egg at dawn.
A dark-lacquered Kunlun man walks through the snow; Turning around, he breaks the lapis lazuli bowl.
Jin-feng was building a roof. The Master asked, "Is it finished? Jin-feng said, "This side is finished. The Master said, "What about that side?
Jin-feng said, "I shall inform the Abbot on the day the work is completed. The Master said, "So it is, so it is."
Question: "A son returns to his father; why does the father not acknowledge him at all? The Master said: "It is only right that it should be so. [The questioner] asked:

"Wherein lies the bond of affection between father and son? The Master said: "Only now is the bond of affection between father and son truly established. [The questioner] asked: "What is this bond of affection between father and son?"
The Master said: "A blade or an axe cannot split it open.
Tiantong commented: "The emerald curtain hangs down; the imperial decree has not yet been issued. The purple silk screen is closed; sight and hearing find no passage.
As soon as a hair-tip moves, the moon rises through the night door. With a subtle shift of one step, the crane emerges from its silver cage. Do you know?"
"Ma! To shed the body into a single color leaves no shadow behind; not to sit within the shared wind fails the great function.
When the Paper-Clothed Ascetic came to visit, the Master asked, "Are you not the Paper-Clothed Ascetic? He replied, "I dare not say so.
The Master asked, "What is the matter beneath the paper cloth? He replied, "Once the single robe is hung upon the body, all phenomena are entirely as they are."
The Master said, "What is the function beneath the paper robe? The student stepped forward, responded with an acknowledgment, and then immediately stood there as if shedding his skin.
The Master said, "You only know how to go like that; you do not know how to come back like this. The student suddenly opened his eyes and asked, "What is the one spiritual true nature?"
"How is it when one does not rely on a womb? The Master said, "That is not yet wondrous. The monk asked, "What is wondrous?

The Master said, "Neither borrowing nor being borrowed from. The monk paid his respects and passed away. The Master presented this verse: "The nature of awakening is perfectly luminous, a formless body;

Do not mistakenly treat it with intimacy or distance through intellectual views. If thoughts differ, the profound essence is obscured; If the mind deviates, it does not dwell as a neighbor to the Way."
When the myriad phenomena of emotional attachments sink into the realm before one, the many facets of discerning consciousness lose their original truth.
If you can fully understand and realize these words, you will clearly see that you are the person of old, free from all affairs.
The "Paper-Clothed Wayfarer" does not rely on the womb; this is precisely a borrowed phrase, precisely a false distancing from what is intimate.
Therefore, Caoshan presented the three characters "not-borrowing-borrowing. Later, he presented a verse that fully elucidates this "not-borrowing-borrowing."
He asked Elder Qiang, “The Buddha’s true Dharma-body is like empty space; it manifests forms in response to things, like the moon reflected in water.
How do you explain this principle of ‘responding’? Qiang said, “It is like a donkey looking down a well.
The Master said, “You have spoken quite a bit, but you have only captured eighty percent of it. Qiang asked, “And how about you, Master? The Master said, “It is like a well looking down at a donkey.”
Question: "What is the lion? The Master said: "No beasts can approach it. Question: "What is the lion’s cub? The Master said: "One who can swallow its parents. Question:

"If you disobey, you shall be executed. The official said, "Disobedience is my duty as a minister; I do not yet know what Your Majesty intends.

"Those in the monastic community who dwell beneath these seams of dharma-garments must understand the matter that transcends them;
do not treat it as trivial. If you are clear in your realization, you can turn all the sages behind yourself. Only then..."
One attains freedom. If one cannot turn it around, then even if one has mastered it to the full extent, one must still stand behind him with palms joined and ask what great talk he is speaking.
If one can turn it around, then when all manner of coarse and heavy circumstances arise, one is able to exercise mastery over them;
even if one falls into the mud, one is still able to maintain mastery. For instance, there was a monk who asked Yushan:

If one remains in the present state, one cannot attain the Buddha-way. What is called a "kalpa" (劫) refers to stagnation. It is termed the "ten accomplishments" (*shicheng*), and is also called "cutting off leakage.
This simply means that the ten paths have been severed. Not forgetting the great fruit, yet remaining stuck in attachment, is called "successively attending to matters.
Upon reaching this point, one must be extremely careful; it makes no difference whether one is in heaven, hell, as a hungry ghost, or an animal.
Birth is merely this: it does not shift across all places; one is fundamentally the same person as before, yet simply does not travel the old path.
If there is a mind of longing, one immediately becomes stuck and attached. If you can break free from this, what is there to choose?
An ancient worthy said, "I only fear that you cannot turn back. What do you say to this? It is just like people nowadays who love to speak of purity and cleanliness. They love...
To speak of past events, this illness is the most difficult to cure. If it were a coarse or heavy worldly matter, it would actually be light; rather, the illness of purity is the heaviest.
Take, for instance, the "flavor of the Buddhas" and the "flavor of the Patriarchs"—these are all attachments. The former master said: "To conceive a thought is to violate the precepts;
to obtain flavor is to break the fast. But what, after all, do you call "flavor"? It is nothing other than the flavor of the Buddhas and the flavor of the Patriarchs. As soon as...

To have a mind of longing is itself a violation of the precepts. As it is said today that one "breaks the fast and breaks the precepts," one does not realize that they were already broken at the moment of the three *karmavācanas*.
If it were greed, anger, or delusion, though difficult to sever, they would still be relatively light.
To be without action, without affairs, and pure—this is heavy; nothing can surpass it. Even when the Patriarchs appeared in the world, it was solely for this reason, and not for anything else.
For you at this time, do not treat this lightly; it would be far better to practice as a black slave or a white ox.
It is not a matter of having Chan or having the Way, nor of your various pursuits—seeking Buddhas, seeking Patriarchs, or even seeking Bodhi and Nirvana.

When will such things ever come to rest and be accomplished? They are all merely the mind of birth and death; therefore, they are not as good as being like a black slave or a white ox, sitting there in simple, steady stillness.
Ignorant. They do not know the Buddha; they do not know the Patriarchs; nor do they know anything from Bodhi and Nirvana down to the causes and effects of good and evil.

They simply eat grass when hungry and drink water when thirsty. If one can act in this manner, there is no need to worry about failing to accomplish the task. It is said that calculating will not succeed;
therefore, one must realize that existence exists, and only then can one don the fur and wear the horns, pull the plow, and drag the harrow. Thus, one attains it.
This is merely expedient; it is only a slight comparison. If you wish to know this matter: even if one were to become a Buddha or a Patriarch, it is still just this.
Even if one were to fall into the three paths and six realms, it is also just this. Although it has no practical use, for now one cannot be separated from it.
One must take mastery over it before it will do. If you can take mastery over it, then that is it.
Transformation and change: if one attempts to exercise mastery over them, one fails; this very failure is itself transformation and change.
As Yongjia said: "Vast and boundless, it invites calamity. [A questioner asks: "What is meant by 'vast and boundless, it invites calamity'? [The Master] says: "This very thing is the whole of it.

Nirvana, afflictions, ignorance, and so forth—none of these are to be avoided. Even coarse and heavy worldly matters, one simply knows they exist and accepts them;
they need not be avoided. To avoid them would be the same as undergoing transformation and change.
This extends even to becoming a Buddha or an Ancestor, or to Bodhi and Nirvana; these calamities are no small matter. Why is this so? It is simply because...
It undergoes transformation; yet, if it were not subject to transformation, one must simply attain freedom in every encounter.

Before the Hall of the Bright Moon stands the Shadowless Tree; On a night of severe frost and snow, it blooms in full flower.

they never act with casual indifference. Even if they speak ten times, they will stop after nine. Why is this so? It is because they fear that there may be no benefit.
For one who has realized the essence, the mind is like a fan in the month of December—until even a film of mold forms upon the lips.
This is not a matter of forced effort; it occurs spontaneously and naturally. To attain such a state, one must be such a person.

how much more so if it is greater? To err by a hair’s breadth is to commit a transgression as vast as a mountain. As the ancients said: "The place of study is not mysterious."
All these are merely worldly conventions; things of the inner chambers that one cannot bear to relinquish, all of which constitute outflows and leaks.
One must directly seize the opportunity right here; whether going or coming, only by exhausting everything at once can one finally be free from fault.

It is like a person who has attained realization in every head and penetration in every object; such a one is merely called a "person of affairs accomplished," but is never called "Noble and Precious.

One should know that the path of the Noble and Precious is distinct by itself; even the most heavy and most precious things in the world cannot be taken toward the side of the Noble and Precious. You must know it is inconceivable. Therefore, the ancients said: "It is just like..."
Two mirrors facing each other, their lights reflecting one another; there is no waxing or waning. Is this not the very same thing?
Yet you still call it a matter of images and reflections. Furthermore, when the sun rises and illuminates the world with clarity, that is one half. What is the other half?

What would you call this? People nowadays have not yet recognized the matter of the gateway of light and shadow; they take it for something belonging to the interior of the house—how could that possibly suffice?
For one who first realized "there is," on the singular path of the Honored One, they remain solely within the realm of images. You must simply...

Chan Master Qinshan Suo was asked by Layman Liang, "What is it like when a single arrowhead breaks through the three barriers?
The Master said, "Let out the master within the barrier and see. Liang said, "If that is so, then one must surely reform one's errors. The Master said, "When do you wait for anything else?"
Liang said, "A fine arrow, but it was not shot into its proper place. He then went out. The Master called, "Come here, Dharma brother! Liang turned his head back.
The Master seized him and said, "Setting aside for a moment the single shaft that pierces the three barriers, let us see you shoot an arrow at Qinshan.
As Liang hesitated, the Master struck him seven blows and said, "Let this fellow go on doubting for thirty years."
Tiantong took up the case, saying: "It comes like mountains piled and peaks heaped; it goes like a wall crumbling and ice melting. Thus people of the age know of its existence.

Can you still realize its essence? If you do not sit upright in the hall, how can you respond to the dualistic mechanisms?
Chan Master Kuangren of Shushan ascended the hall and said: "This sick monk understood the affairs of the Dharma-side before the Xiantong era."
After the year of Xiantong, he attained the realization of that which transcends the Dharma-body. Yunmen came forward and asked, "What is the matter of the Dharma-body?
The Master said, "A withered stump. [Yunmen] asked, "What is the matter that transcends the Dharma-body? The Master said, "Not a withered stump."

[The student] asked, "Is that which is not a withered stump not a matter pointing toward what is above the Dharma-body? The Master said, "It is."
The Master said, “It does. [The monk] asked, “In that case, does the Dharmakāya encompass all things? The Master said, “The Dharmakāya is all-pervasive; how could it not encompass them?

"The Dharma-body is certainly without 'upward' or 'downward'; it is only because you perceive distinctions between the near and the distant that you speak thus."

however, for this sick monk, it is not so. Gushan asked, "What is the Teacher, King Vairocana Buddha? The Master said, "Not..."
He sat in no noble position.
Lingquan asked, "A withered tree blossoming with flowers—this begins to accord with others. Is this a statement of 'this side' or a statement of 'that side'?
The Master said, "It is also a statement of 'this side. Lingquan asked, "What is a statement of 'that side'? The Master said, "The stone ox spits forth..."
Fog in the third month of spring. The numinous magpie does not perch in the shadowless forest;

withered wood produces flowers—this is precisely the matter of merit on this side. The two lines regarding the stone ox spitting mist are the manifestation of function upon returning from that side; what is called "the merit of no-merit."

Chan Master Qinglin Shiguan. A monk asked, "What is it like when a student goes directly forward? The Master said, "A dead snake lies across the main road;

The monk asked, "What happens if one does not step over it? The Master said, "There is likewise no place to avoid it. The monk asked, "At such a time as this..."

Dana’s verse says: The long river is clear and transparent, reflecting the moon’s brilliance; Yet this pervasive clarity is not yet the home.
I ask: where does the fisherman’s boat go? At nightfall, it remains as before, moored among the reeds.
Tiantong’s verse says: The three elders secretly turn the rudder; The solitary boat turns its head at night. Reeds and flowers are snow upon both banks;
Mist and waters are autumn across the river. The wind’s power holds the sail, traveling without rowing; The sound of the flute calls one down to the moonlit isles.
One day, National Teacher Hyujeong of the Huayan tradition struck the gavel and said, "Those in the upper quarters shall carry firewood; those in the lower quarters shall hoe the fields.
A head seat asked, "What is the Holy Monk doing? The Master replied, "He does not sit upright in the hall; how could he attend to the dual functions at both ends?"
Master Qianfeng ascended the hall and said: "The Dharma-body has three kinds of illnesses and two kinds of radiance;
you must penetrate each one thoroughly before you can understand how to return home and sit in peace. You must know that there is yet another opening beyond this. Yunmen stepped forward and asked:
"Those inside the hermitage—why do they not know what happens outside? The Master laughed heartily. Baizhang said, "This is still a point of doubt for students.
The Master asked, "What kind of mental activity is yours? Baizhang said, "I also wish for the Master to understand me."
The Master said, "You must simply act this way before you can sit securely. The Gatekeeper responded, "Yes, yes.
Addressing the assembly, the Master said, "If you raise one, you must not raise two. To let one point pass is to fall into the second.
Yunmen stepped forward from the assembly and said, "Yesterday someone came from Tiantai and went on to Jingshan. The Master said, "Tomorrow..."
Having obtained the general invitation, he then descended from his seat.

Tiantong took up the case, saying: "When sitting and cutting off the ten directions, a thousand divergent paths are severed; when letting loose a single thread, ten thousand streams flow toward the source.
Only when these two venerable masters open up their family style can one truly see the comings and goings of a monk. Do you understand this clearly? Tai...
The Emperor’s decree pervades the realm; the General’s heart lies beyond the frontier.
Master Bao’ai was asked by a monk, “When the world is destroyed, where does this thing go? The Master said, “Not even a thousand sages can find it.
The monk asked, “How then do people of the present age turn toward it? The Master said, “You must become just like it. The monk asked, “Is there still anyone who attains it?”...
[The student] said, "It is truly so. The Master said, "I do not establish any fixed standard.
Chan Master Jiufeng Tongxuan instructed his disciples, saying: "The intent of the Buddhas and the intent of the Patriarchs are like the opening and closing of one's hand.
The former master established the Five Ranks to clarify the fundamental principle of Yunyan; it is like a divine physician treating an illness—the medicine is simply this."

For those who practice in daily life: regarding speech, avoid being overly definitive; one does not wish to sever the continuity [of the Dharma]. Regarding the mind, avoid provocation or offense; one does not wish to defile it.
Yet, those who study [the Way] possess minds that are not yet subtle; they seek only the "Nine-Revolution Elixir," claiming it can raise the dead.

This is most certainly not so. Within the *Lotus Sūtra*, there is the chapter on the "Transformed City. The Buddhas and Patriarchs spoke of this in secret. Read it thoroughly and clearly; its great penetration is manifest.

The Buddha Jñānavijaya sat at the site of enlightenment. Having defeated the armies of Māra and being on the verge of attaining anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, the dharmas of all Buddhas did not appear before him.

In this manner, for one intermediate kalpa, and even up to ten intermediate kalpas, he remained seated in the full lotus posture, his body and mind unmoving, yet the dharmas of all Buddhas still did not appear before him. As for the phrase "on the verge of attaining," it means:
A small kalpa. To speak of "ten small kalpas" refers to that which is defiled and that which is severed. It is further said:
"The Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū, after ten small kalpas had passed, the Dharma of all Buddhas appeared before him, and he attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The phrase "after ten small kalpas had passed" conveys the principle of the mutual interplay between the provisional and the ultimate. The Patriarch said: "Relying upon..."
How could it not be so regarding the awakening to the essence of the teaching?

When Xuanchu of Jiufeng first visited Deshan, Deshan alone regarded him as extraordinary; yet he had not yet attained great penetration. Later, upon meeting Dongshan, he realized the ultimate meaning.
Dongshan said: "One holds a divine pearl in the palm and displays it to people in broad daylight, yet they still draw their swords against it—how much more so for Xuanchu?"
"Is it night? You may be considered noble. The Master said, "It is simply that you do not recognize the pearl. Once recognized, there is neither day nor night. Jia praised him as a man of talent.
After Jia passed away, he lived in a hut beside the stupa. By the beginning of the Zhonghe era, he took his leave of the stupa and traveled north.
Observing the entirety of this relationship between teacher and disciple from beginning to end, one cannot say that he did not deeply attain [the truth].
This is the essential point. This passage is omitted in all other records; only Juefan included it within his *Sengbao zhuan* (Biographies of the Jewel of the Sangha).
Regarding the language, he avoided reaching full completion so as not to sever the continuity; regarding the pivot of the teaching (*ji*), he avoided direct confrontation so as not to defile it.

He elucidated the Master’s intent with concise yet exhaustive phrasing and cited scriptures to establish its validity. It originally derives from the *Baoming sanmei* (Treasure Mirror Samādhi), and Caoshan also...
There is an illuminating passage that differs slightly from this; let the observer examine it closely.
When Master Chan Master Jiǔfēng Dàoqián was asked by the assembly to succeed [the abbot] after Shíshuāng had passed away, the Master said:
"You must first understand the meaning of the former master before you can proceed. The student asked, "What was the former master’s meaning? The Master said, "The former master said:
'Rest! Cease! Be cold and still! A single thought for ten thousand years! A single strand of white silk!'"
He did not ask about anything else. [The Master asked: "What is it like to go as a single strand of white silk? Zuo said, "This merely clarifies matters on the side of 'one color'.
The Master said, "So you have not yet understood the intention of our former teacher. Zuo said, "Do you not accept me? Just bring some incense.
When the smoke of the incense is cut off, if you cannot go, then you have not understood the intention of our former teacher. Thereupon—

He burned incense. Before the smoke had even faded, the Master had already passed away while seated. The teacher patted his back and said, "It is not that he did not 'pass away while sitting' or 'perish while standing,' yet he has not even dreamed of the meaning of our former master."
Tiantong’s Verse says: The school of Shishuang was personally transmitted by Jiufeng. When the incense smoke vanished, the true pulse became difficult to penetrate.
The crane in its moon-nest dreams of a thousand years; The person in the snow-house is lost in the function of the single color.
Severing the ten directions, he still receives a mark on his forehead; He shifts a step in secret—watch the flying dragon.
Question: I have heard it said in the past that "to succeed by turning outward is the rank of a minister; to succeed by turning inward is the lineage of a king.

Is this so? The Master said: "It is. [The questioner] asked: "What is succeeding by turning outward? The Master said: "If one does not know the ultimate limit of affairs, one merely manages the affairs themselves."
"This is called 'external succession' (wài-shào); this is the lineage of the ministers. [The student] asked, "What is 'internal succession' (nèi-shào)?
The Master said, "To know how to take responsibility and bear the burden within; this is internal succession. [The student] asked, "What is the 'royal lineage' (wáng-zhòng)?

The Master said, "One must see the person who has no one to take responsibility for and no burden to bear; only then does one attain the same color. Once the same color is attained, for this reason, one borrows [the name]."
"To bring about birth. This is the royal lineage. [The student] said, "If that is so, then the inner succession must also undergo transformation.

The Master said, "It is certainly true that there is one who can accept and carry this burden; how could it not be transformed? You say that the inner succession is precisely the seed of the human king.
But tell me, do you think there is still any principle of 'succession' at present? Therefore, the ancients said: "Succession is a function; succession..."
"Realizing that it is not a matter of effort, one turns effort back to its fundamental station; only then is one called a member of the royal lineage. [The student] asked:

"I do not yet understand whether those who 'succeed externally' also undergo this turning back? The Master said: "Those who succeed externally have not yet known that [the Way] exists at all; for now, we must simply teach them to know that it exists.
[The student] asked: "What is it to know that it exists? The Master said: "At dawn, one does not realize it is already light."

Question: "What is 'external succession'? The Master said: "Not borrowing another person's household affairs. Question: "What is 'internal succession'? The Master said: "Pushing the father toward the interior. Question:
"Between these two statements, which one is most intimate? The Master said: "The minister is within the gate; the king does not go out the gate. Question:
"If that is so, then he who does not go out the gate does not fall into either of the two extremes. The Master— [remained silent].
It is said: "He does not sit alone within the world; internally he succeeds to the royal lineage, and externally he succeeds to the royal clan.

Therefore it is said: 'Succeeding' refers to the achievement of fame and merit. 'Minister' is the state of being centered within the partial. Having succeeded, one transforms fame and merit. 'Ruler' is the state of being partial within the center."
"The minister is within the gate; the King does not go out the gate. Both point and push the father toward the interior.
This "minister" refers to the Prince, not an external minister. Regarding the names for those who succeed the royal lineage internally and those who succeed the royal clan externally:
it is clear that Shishuang’s establishment of the five princes actually involves distinctions. Those who succeed internally merely obtain the name; those who succeed externally [obtain the clan].
This merely refers to obtaining his surname. One must succeed to and transform one's merit before becoming a true prince. This succession of merit is "inner succession" (neishao).
If inner succession has not yet transformed [into mastery], one remains in the rank of a minister; this is entirely partial, for it is based on the knowledge that there is something [to attain].
It is "purity within partiality. Only when succession is complete and merit is transformed does one become of royal lineage. Why is such a person called a ruler? Because...
Regarding his position as the Crown Prince: this is "the partial within the central. This differs from what Dongshan established. [A monk] asked:
"Does the newborn still know or hear anything? The Master said: "Who else would he know or hear? [The monk] said:
"If that is so, does it not mean it is exactly thus? The Master said: "If it were so, why did the ancients say, 'King Birth has a father'? [The monk] said: "Since..."
"There is a father. Why do you not know or hear of him? The Master said, "At the same time, he does not recognize the Patriarch.
[The student] asked, "An ancient said, 'Even one who does not come in such a way is still a descendant.
What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "The ancients did not speak falsely. [The student] asked, "What is a descendant who does not come in such a way? The Master said, "Still..."
Shouzhen was attending him. [Shouzhen] asked, "What is the father? The Master said, "There is no house where one may sit;
there is no world from which one may arise. A monk asked, "What is the head? The Master said, "Opening one's eyes, one does not see the dawn. [The monk] asked, "What is the tail? The Master said:
[The Master] did not sit upon the "Ten-Thousand-Year Bed. [A monk] asked, "What is it like when there is a head but no tail? The Master said, "In the end, it is not noble.
[The monk] asked, "What is it like when there is a tail but no head? The Master said, "Though full, one has no strength. [The monk] asked, "What is it like when the head and tail match?
The Master said, "The descendants have the power; those inside the room do not know."
Tiantong’s verse says: "Ruler for the circle, carpenter’s square for the square; To act, to travel, to rest, or to hide. Leaving the bird dwelling in the reeds at its wits' end;
The sheep advancing or retreating, caught against the fence. Eating the food of others, sleeping on one's own bed. Clouds rise to bring rain; dew凝结 (coagulates) to become frost.
Jade threads meet and pass through the eye of the needle; Silken threads unbroken emerge from the loom’s heart. The stone woman’s shuttle—"
The night lingers as it approaches midnight; the wooden man turns his path as the moonlight shifts to its center.
A monk asked Master Puzhao of Shaoshan, "In a place where right and wrong do not reach, is there still a phrase? The Master said, "There is."
The monk asked, "What kind of phrase is this? The Master said, "A single mass of white clouds does not reveal its ugliness.
Tiantong took up the case and said: "His entire being shifts and turns; he avoids touching upon the dignified majesty. Stepping back from his position, he raises it from the side;
he must indeed be skillfully evasive. Do you see how Shaoshan acted for him? With all his might, he pushes his father toward the interior."
Touzi’s verse says: The white clouds do not reach the summit of the central peak; The landscape of misty vines fills the eyes, extraordinary.
A single phrase contains the melody of a thousand ages; Amidst ten thousand layers of azure green, the moon first arrives.
Master Jingxin of Yongquan ascended the hall and said: "I have been here for forty-nine years, yet I still occasionally stumble.
You people must not open your mouths too wide. Those with intellectual understanding are many, but among ten thousand, there is not one who possesses both realization and conduct.
Intellectual views and verbal expressions all require thorough mastery; if your recognition is not complete, I dare say you will remain in the cycle of rebirth."
You need only exhaust the present moment for it to be established; this is called "achieving merit within standing.

To turn that merit over to him is called "achieving merit within approaching," which is to approach him intimately. This is why I say: "The person you are intimate with cannot be saved, nor can he save the one you are intimate with.
Even with such a metaphor, you still do not understand how to take it up. You merely go on swallowing it whole. Just keep taking it up!
Your nature is distracted and your tongue flutters; you do not see the Way of Dongshan. Continuity is also most difficult.
You must know that such a thing exists; if you do not know that such a thing exists, there will be days of weeping.
This marks the exhaustion of the present moment; it is precisely the time for "turning the function to abide in the position," not referring to the final entry or the attainment of the station.
The practitioner of Hekxi was looking at Luopu when he asked: "Since we parted at Lixi, how many years have passed now?"
Xixun said, "Master, you still remember the events of the past. Puhua said, "I have heard it said that those who speak of the Way forget dates and years altogether.
Xixun said, "The Master’s duties as abbot are many; allow me to consider this carefully. Puhua said, "If you strike, strike a man who understands Chan.
Xixun said, "That would not be necessary either. Puhua said, "The practitioner’s affairs of mountain dwelling are many."
Danxia’s verse says: Such news as this is no ordinary matter; The branches of the moon-blossomed cassia spread their fragrance afar.
Last night, the Lady Chang’e displayed her ingenuity; Her eyes were embroidered with mandarin ducks soaring upward.

Chan Master Yunmen Wenyan said: "When light does not penetrate through, there are two kinds of illnesses. First, there is the lack of clarity in all places, as if there were an object before one's face.
Second, having penetrated through so that all phenomena are empty, there is still a lingering sense, as if there were some kind of thing remaining."
This, too, is a case where the light has not yet penetrated through. Furthermore, the Dharma-body also has two kinds of illnesses.
First, having attained the Dharma-body, one fails to forget the attachment to dharmas; one's own views still persist, and one falls into the side of the Dharma-body.
This is the first. Even if you manage to penetrate it, do not let it pass unexamined. If you scrutinize it closely, what trace of life is there? That, too, is an illness.
The Chan Master Gaetong of Shizhu traveled to Dongshan. At that time, Master Qian uttered a teaching statement, saying: "There are four kinds of people.

One person has surpassed the Buddhas and patriarchs in their discourse, yet cannot take a single step in practice. Another person has surpassed the Buddhas and patriarchs in their practice, yet cannot utter a single word in discourse.
Another person can both discourse and practice. And another person can neither discourse nor practice. Which one is it?"

"This is that person. The Master stepped forward from the assembly and said: "The one who has surpassed the Buddhas and Patriarchs in speech but cannot take a single step—this is simply because he lacks a tongue and is not permitted to walk.
The one who has surpassed the Buddhas and Patriarchs in walking but cannot utter a single word—this is simply because he lacks feet and is not permitted to speak.
The one who can both speak and walk is merely like a box and its lid fitting perfectly together. As for the fourth person—"
"To say it cannot be attained and to act it cannot be practiced is like seeking life after one's breath has been cut off; this is like the son of a barren woman wearing a cangue and shackles.
Yunshan asked, "What about your own portion, Master? The Master said, "In my own portion, everything is thoroughly penetrated;
how could it fail to be manifest? Yunshan asked, "But what about Minggong Xiù of Haishang? How is he? The Master said, "When illusory people meet, they clap their hands."
Hehe. In the first two cases, there is correctness but no partiality; in the third, there is partiality but no correctness; and in the fourth, both partiality and correctness are absent.

Therefore, in all these instances, they are not the true person. As for "how could the outstanding brilliance ever be manifest?"—this means that partiality is not absolute partiality. This is the Honorable Master Ming of Haishang.
"Xiu! Half-light, half-dark—this is the mark of partiality that is not entirely partial. When illusory people meet, they clap their hands and laugh 'he-he.
This is a statement that clarifies while simultaneously encompassing both."
Danxia’s verse says: An ox of mud plows the white moon beneath the water; A wooden horse gallops through the clear wind amidst the clouds.
The barbarian monk is too lazy to hold the bowl of the Western Heaven; At midnight, he boards a boat and crosses over to the eastern sea.
Chan Master Jinfeng Congzhi was asked by a monk, "What is the true master of Jinfeng? The Master said, "The county seat is not far from here;
do not act so hastily, O *ācārya*. The monk asked, "Why do you not speak? The Master replied, "My mouth is like a foundation stone."
Chan Master Cheng Huguo was asked by a monk, "What is one's original father and mother? The Master said, "He whose head does not turn white.
The monk asked, "With what do you offer them? The Master said, "Diligently served rice-free gruel; before the hall, no inquiry about kin."
Danxia’s verse says: Stepping out the door, the entire world lacks a true friend; Entering the house, what meets the eyes is no kinsman.
In the empty chamber, cold at night, what is there? The bright moon in the blue sky serves as my neighbor.
Chan Master Xianyun of Shimen was serving as a garden head at Qinglin. One day, while standing in attendance, Qinglin asked, "What have you been doing today?
The Master replied, "I have been planting vegetables. Qinglin said, "The entire world is the Buddha-body; where do you plant?
The Master said, "The golden hoe does not move the earth; the spiritual sprouts grow wherever they are. Qinglin was pleased.
Chan Master Tong’an Zhi was at Tong’an. When he learned that [Master] Wei was about to pass away, he ascended the hall and said:
“Before the Many-Son Stupa, the lineage heir is outstanding; before the Five Old Peaks, what of the matter? He raised this three times, but none offered a response.

Finally, the Master [Zhi] stepped forward and said: “Standing in formation outside the curtain of night-brightness, ten thousand miles of song and chant proclaim the Great Peace. Wei said: “It must be...”
"This donkey-like fellow has finally got it!
This is the ultimate teaching of the Caodong school. Later generations, however, possess inferior and shallow capacities;

they do not understand the non-action (*wuwei*) of Yao and Shun, but instead boast grandly about the military conquests and punishments of Tang and Wu. They even presume that Yao and Shun were inferior to Tang and Wu."
How lamentable!
A monk asked, "When the two capacities do not reach [the truth], how should one proclaim it? The Master said, "Not encountered anywhere; not lost within the profound."
Danxia’s verse says: On this side or that, it is difficult to encounter; A single word, free from self-interest, does not abide in the center.
The crimson sun sinks behind the western peaks, Leaving but its solitary shadow reaching to the east of the stream.
The Chan Master Shimen Huiche. Once, Hualiang Long asked him, "An ancient said, 'If one can simply find peace and ease wherever one is, one will naturally accord with the tracks of the ancients.
Although these words exist, my doubts have not yet ceased. What do you say? The Master said, "One must know that there is [the Way] before one can find peace and ease wherever one is.
It is like a person living in a prefecture or a county who, whether hearing or seeing, encounters a thousand wonders and a hundred marvels."

How strange! He always treats it as ordinary; he does not realize its existence, yet remains at ease. It is like a person living in a village who, upon encountering a slight sound or sight, becomes startled and spreads rumors about it.
Formerly, Dongshan instructed the assembly, saying: "If you wish to know this matter, it is like a family raising three sons:
one is stationed in the prefecture, one in the county, and one in the village. One of them uses the family's resources."
Regarding money and goods: one uses money and goods from outside; there is another person who may neither use money and goods from within the house nor use money and goods from outside.
Tell me, which of these three should be placed in the prefecture, which in the county, and which in the village?
A monk then asked: "Do these three people not clearly understand the relative weight [of their circumstances]?"
"No. [The Master] said, "Yes. The monk asked, "What is the place where one born among the people of the county emerges?

[The Master] said, "To know that there is, yet not to know that there is—this is the place where this person emerges. The monk asked, "I do not know for certain: does this person depart from this very day or not?

[The Master] said, "He also departs from this very day. The monk said, "If that is so, then he belongs to the realm of effort (*puṇya*). [The Master] said, "Yes. The monk asked, "What would you call him?"
Mogong said, "I call it the merit of having accomplished the work. The monk asked, "Do you recognize anyone from within the prefecture?

Mogong replied, "I recognize them. [The monk said,] "Only then can one be said to pay due respect. The monk said, "If that is so, then those from the village have fully understood their transgression.
Mogong said, "Yes. The monk asked, "What is this person’s point of transgression? Mogong said, "Not knowing 'there is'—this is called being a common man. This is it.
"Where people pass through, they do not see the Way of the former masters. Those who study the Way today must know that there is a place for turning the body before they can succeed.
Long then asked, "If the ancients knew this, were they able to act like a person from the prefecture? Or must it also be attained through the weight of formal service?
The Master then cited the Five Ranks of Merit (*wǔ wèi gōngxūn*) and further said, "It is like a young dove that has just hatched."
The feathers of this creature are pitiable; yet after a long time, it will naturally be able to fly high and soar far.
Those within the village do not know it exists; those within the district know it exists; those within the prefecture know it exists but do not truly realize its presence.
When those within the district first come to know it exists, it is like using money from one's own household.
Regarding "objects": these refer to expenditures made beyond the boundaries of the community.
Since those within the village are unaware of such things, they possess no corresponding capacity for engagement; therefore, neither the internal nor external funds of the household may be used.
Chan Master Guangde Zhou was asked by a monk, "In the midst of waves and billows, how can one attain the wondrous?
The Master said, "Without employing oars or paddles, and with the bottom removed, one's coming and going never requires a life-preserving float."
Danxia’s verse says: A single phrase in response is difficult to grasp; The Wheel-Turning King does not transform the land of Jambudvīpa.
In boundless lands, the waves of the ocean are level; Riding alone upon a mud ox, he plows the moonlight.
Chan Master Yanguan Yuan asked a monk, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "At midnight, a tortoise wears snow upon its head; at dawn, a mute man returns home with it in his arms."
Dana’s verse says: Auspicious mists and auspicious smoke lock the Jade Tower; The Prince in his prime wanders at leisure.
Upon the crystal palace he rides a golden horse; Before the Hall of the Bright Moon he rolls a brocade ball.
Chan Master Lian-shan Yuan-guan was asked by a monk, "What is it like when the 'house-thief' is difficult to guard against?
The Master said, "If you recognize him, he is no longer an enemy. The monk asked, "After recognizing him, what then? The Master said, "Exile him to the realm of non-arising.

The monk asked, "Is this not where he establishes his dwelling and sustains his life? The Master said, "A stagnant pool does not harbor dragons. The monk asked, "What is a dragon of the living waters? The Master— [continued].
[The monk] said, "Raising waves without creating ripples. [The Master] asked, "What about when the pools suddenly overflow and the peaks collapse?
The Master descended from his seat, seized him, and said, "Do not let it soak the corner of this old monk's kashaya."
A monk asked the Master, "What is the matter of daily life? The Master said, "Jade-green beryl pierces through the color of lapis lazuli;
though red dust fills the eyes, not a grain of sand is seen."
Danxia’s verse says: The kalpa-fire blazes forth, yet it is the abode of formlessness; At the golden gates, one beholds no imperial palace.
In the jewel-sky, clouds are thin and the Milky Way is cold; In the vast surging waves, how could the sands be moved?
A monk asked, "What is the matter prior to the empty kalpa? The Master said, "The drum that shakes heaven and earth is struck;
people of the time do not hear it. Danxia’s verse says: "Empty space is the drum, Mount Sumeru the mallet; though those who strike it are many, those who hear it are few. Half... [verse continues].
At night, the skull startles the dream; with the bright moon filling his head, he has no thought of returning.
Zen Master Dayang Jingxuan asked Liangshan, "What is the formless site of enlightenment?
Liangshan pointed to an image of Avalokiteśvara and said, "This one was painted by Wu Daozi. As the Master hesitated, Liangshan urgently demanded, "This one is—"
"The one with marks—how about the one without marks? At these words, the Master attained realization. He prostrated, rose, returned to his place, and stood there.
Yunmen said, "Why do you not utter a single phrase? The Master replied, "I would not decline to speak, but I fear it would merely take up paper and ink."
Shanxiao said, "These words shall be inscribed upon stone. Later, they were indeed carved upon a stele.

While Shen Cheng the attendant was standing in attendance, the Master said, "There is a person whose entire body is red and festering, lying amidst a thicket of thorns, surrounded on all sides by fire.
If you can approach this person, he will open wide his marketplace for you; if you cannot approach him..."

"Attainable. [The Master asked: "What do you take as the standard for this time? Cheng said, "Only those whose six sense organs are incomplete and whose seven consciousnesses are not whole can begin to draw near and attain it.
The Master said, "Have him come out; I wish to see him. Cheng said, "Just now there was no one else present to respond to the Master.
The Master said, "An official does not allow even a needle to pass. Cheng then prostrated himself.
Dayang said, "I wish to see him. The appropriate answer would have been: "He has never seen a guest since time immemorial.
Chan Master Touzi Yiqing ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying: "If one discusses this matter, it is like a phoenix soaring to the heavens, leaving no trace;
or a wild goat hanging from a horn, where can its tracks be found? A golden dragon does not remain in the cold pool."
How could the jade hare ever dwell within the shadow of the moon? Should host and guest stand facing one another, they must shake their heads beyond the world of Vairocana.
When questions and answers are set forth, they must be raised as a direct call from the side of the profound path. If you can do so, you are still only halfway there;
if you look on with fixed eyes, there is no need for us to meet at all.
Danxia’s verse says: The water is clear and the moon is full, yet the man of the Way feels sorrow. The wondrous exhaustion is without reliance; categories cannot be gathered.
Beyond the kalpas lie the paths of the orthodox and the biased combined; One discerns spring and autumn upon the branch that never sprouts.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "In a solitary village or a humble inn, do not hang up your water jar or alms bowl. At the profound barrier of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, pass straight through with body outstretched.
This is already like Su Wu crossing the frontier, where the path sought is difficult to return from; it is like Xiang Yu facing the river, where how could one escape a life of exhaustion?

O Zen practitioners, having arrived here, to advance is to fall into the realm of celestial Māras; to retreat is to sink into the destiny of ghosts. Neither advancing nor retreating—this is precisely..."
"In the waters of death. O worthy ones, how can you attain stability? After a long silence, he said: "Let the snow fall three feet deep;
it cannot suppress a single inch of the spiritual pine."
Chan Master Xingyang Qingpou was serving as the head gardener at Dayang. While he was planting melons, Dayang asked, "When will the sweet melons ripen?
The Master replied, "They have already ripened and rotted away. Dayang said, "Pick out the sweet ones and bring them here.
The Master asked, "For whom would you eat them? Dayang said, "For those who do not enter the garden. The Master asked, "I wonder, does that one who does not enter the garden eat them or not?"
Yang said, "Do you still recognize him? The Master replied, "Although I do not recognize him, I cannot help but give it to him.
Dayang smiled and departed.
A monk asked, "When Sāgara emerges from the sea and heaven and earth tremble, what is the matter when face is presented directly? The Master said, "The Golden-Winged Bird."
The Bird-King presides over the universe. Among these, who is the one who emerges? [A monk] asked: "If one suddenly encounters the moment of emergence, what then?
The Master said: "It is like a hawk seizing a pigeon; you may not believe it, but only when you verify it before a skull will you know it is true.
[The monk] said: "In that case, I shall fold my hands at my chest and retreat three paces. The Master said: "The tortoise beneath the seat of Mount Sumeru."

Chan Master Baofeng Chanti Weizhao had five sets of dharma-talks that revealed his fundamental principle and entrusted them to the Librarian Cong.
The first says: "Caoshan established four prohibitions that constitute the very life-vein of all patch-robed monks. If you can penetrate through them, you must by all means avoid relying [on them]."
Relying on what has been handed down: one who has settled the matter must have a separate path of vital energy. Second: "A patch-robed monk walks among those of different species.
The former masters said, "Falling into the category of 'different species'—this is the sickness of one who has settled the matter.

Ming'an said, "One must recognize the master before it can be attained. Third: "An icchantika (one who lacks the seeds of enlightenment) usually tells people: 'You cannot practice Chan; you cannot study [the Way].'"

The Buddha said: "It is only because he is like one who has died the great death. If he had truly died, he would never consent to such a view.
When you act as a teacher for others in the future, you must be extremely careful. Fourth, it is said: "My school establishes the Five Ranks as its fundamental principle; often..."

People clarify it through principle and phenomena; they harmonize it through stillness and illumination; they perceive it through subject and object; they understand it through essence and function. Thus, everything falls entirely into the present moment.

When Chan Master Dayong of Qi’an ascended the hall, he said: "The principle of pure emptiness is where Buddhas and Patriarchs alike return; ultimately, there is no body."
The sage and the ordinary person are of one essence; this is the principle. But as for the myriad phenomena arrayed before one’s eyes—how is their functioning?

When even a speck of dust is cut off from its limits, those who possess the eye do not look on from the side. Official business does not admit a needle; private matters allow for carriages and horses.
If you reach such a state, only then can you respond to conditions and make use of things as they come to hand. Wondrously responding without fixed method, you walk the mysterious path in the wind.
One has directly attained the golden needle and brocade seam, yet the traces of the thread are not revealed; the jade palace and jeweled steps stand, yet the pearl curtains have not been rolled back.
At this very moment, tell me: what kind of realm is this? On the ancient ferry, the autumn wind blows cold and whistling; red pampas grass and purple smartweed fill the bends of the river.

The entire body is unobstructed; letting go of the hand, one is free from reliance. The stone woman ascends the loom at night; the secret chamber has no one to sweep it.
At such a time, how can you entrust yourself to a single word that cuts off the breath? After a long silence, he said: "Returning to the root, the wind causes the leaves to fall."
The moon illuminates the entire pond until it is empty.
He asked a monk, "In the crystal palace, the jade maidens ply their shuttles; what matter of clarity is this? The monk said, "Reciprocity is not appropriate for the immediate occasion.
The Master said, "Is there still continuity or interruption here? The monk said, "From ancient times to the present, there has never been an interval. The Master said, "Precisely at that moment..."
A monk asked, "How is it when there is an interval? The monk said, "I respectfully take my leave," and departed.
Chan Master Tiantong Zhengjue was asked by a monk, "When the principle of pure emptiness ultimately has no body, what then?
The Master said, "Before a trace of pattern appears, the message is difficult to transmit. The monk said, "With a single step, the subtle path shifts; it penetrates."
"The body is cast down, and the kalpa-jar is empty. The Master said, "When birth accords with the father, the entire substance is without omission or illumination.

[The student] asked, "If the principle is thus, what of the phenomena? The Master said, "As each thing returns clearly, it differentiates into myriad affairs; how could responding to the capacities of the ten directions be any hindrance?
[The student] said, "In that case, every dust mote manifests the original body. The Master said, "It penetrates all things."

"Form transcends all mind; this is called knowing things according to their true principle. [The student] asked, "And how about this? The Master said, "When you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not strike it;

The Master said, "The wooden man sings atop the ridge; the stone woman dances by the stream."

The elder Chan Master Jingshen Dasi first went to visit Chanti Zhao. Zhao said, "You must directly sever the thoughts of arising and ceasing, clear away the subtle paths prior to the empty kalpa, and not involve yourself with the orthodox or the biased.
Exhaust the present moment and let go of yourself entirely; having let go completely, let go once more, and only then will you have a share in freedom.
Upon hearing this, the Master suddenly awakened to its essential meaning. Zhao then beat the drum and announced [his realization].
The assembly said, "He has deeply realized the way of the icchantika’s great death; students should rely upon this. Consequently, he was titled "The Elder of Great Death" (Dasi Weng).

When Master Wen’an heard of this, he succeeded to the lineage of Chan Master Zong. A monk asked, "What is it to turn function into position? The Master said, "Casting off the hand, there is no dependence;
the whole body is manifest. A lone boat, a fisherman, sleeps among the reeds. The monk asked, "What is it to turn position into function? The Master—
[The student] asked: "At midnight, the wind and moon atop the ridge are still; a single cry rings out from an old monkey in a high tree. [The student] asked:
"What is 'merit and rank both manifest'? The Master said: "Leaving the gate, one does not tread the path by which one came; the dust before one's eyes flies, yet there is not a speck of grime.
[The student] asked: "What is 'merit and rank both hidden'? The Master said: "The clay ox drinks up the moon over the clear pool; the stone horse receives the lash of the whip."
He did not nod his head.
One night, Chan Master Jixiang Yuanshi attained a realization. At dawn, he went to the abbot’s quarters.
Upon seeing him, Tianyi asked, "How do you explain the Five Ranks of Dongshan? The Master replied, "In my place, there is not even a single rank. Tianyi ordered him to attend the hall.
He said to his attendant, "This man indeed possesses a point of view; it is only a pity that he does not recognize the fundamental principle (zongzhi).

On the occasion of entering the room for instruction, Yunmen had five people arrange themselves in order beforehand. When the Master arrived, he summoned them all by their titles of "Senior Seat" (shangzu).

Thereupon, [Fengxue] secretly grasped the essence of the teaching and uttered this verse: "The single rank is just revealed, and the five ranks are distinguished; When ruler and subject are in harmony, purple clouds gather. At night..."
The bright curtain rolls up, illuminating all without partiality; the golden halls, layer upon layer, reveal the Supreme Honored One. His celestial robes are most fitting.
This is the essential secret of Master Shantang Chun of the New Feng lineage, which branches from the "Lotus-Jade" stream. It began with passing the water and encountering the person;

through this wondrous vision, one perceives the inanimate preaching the Dharma. Now, without being touched, he extends his hand to penetrate the profound mystery, arranging the five ranks of the orthodox and the biased.
It divides into three kinds of permeation: beyond the curtains of the night’s clarity, the minister withdraws from his station to attend the sovereign;
before the ancient mirror-stand, the child turns his body to approach the father. Snow covers the paths of the ten-thousand-year pines; at midnight, there is perfect brightness.

Clouds veil a range of peaks; when day breaks, they are not revealed. The pivot of the Way is subtle and dense; the realm of wisdom is deep and vast. It silently illumines the time prior to the kalpa of emptiness, profoundly still...

In the profound unity of wind and moon within a single pitcher, one sits through to the other side of Vipaśyin Buddha. With clear, translucent mist and light filling the eyes, flowers bloom upon buds that never sprouted;
phoenixes dance atop trees that cast no shadow. With no trace of the shuttle or loom, there lies the pair of golden needles within;
with patterns flowing freely, the jade thread is secretly threaded therein. When the two luminosities arise in mutual confrontation, one knows there is something natural.

When the sudden arrival of the "double-belted" [guest] occurs upon the withered tree, one is finally able to act as the master. Without abiding in the orthodox position, how could one concern oneself with the Great Function?

Reaching the exhaustion of the present moment, how could there be room for honor or nobility? Cutting off the dust of emotions and the net of views, pulling open the golden lock of the mysterious pass, the wondrous embrace is fully opened.
Clearly manifesting while mingling within the categories, the level mind is ever real; brilliantly hidden within the embers, the scroll is unrolled.

Relaxing, yet not failing to manifest his meritorious achievements; coming and going, there is no change or alteration. If one wishes to cause the extraordinary sprouts to flourish, it depends on the preciousness of deeply rooting the spiritual source.
Were it not for the rustic man of Chai-shi (Chai-shi being the alternative name of Fushan Yuan), how could one have seen this "New Feng" song?
Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin said: "Dongshan called it the place of non-alteration, where there is no Buddha, no sentient beings, no right or wrong, and no good or evil;
it is utterly devoid of sound and trace. Thus he said: 'Gold dust is a cataract in the eye; the pearl in one's clothing is but a speck on the Dharma.
If one does not even value one’s own spiritual nature, what are the Buddhas and Patriarchs? This is penetrating in every way—its supernatural powers."

This wondrous function is not something extraordinary. When one reaches this point, with a tattered robe covering the head, all affairs come to rest; at such a time, even this mountain monk knows nothing of it.
The sun and moon revolve through the great void, never ceasing for a moment. It is not that I say I possess these many names and forms; Heaven is universal.
The earth universally supports and nurtures all things, yet it does not say, "I possess such great merit and practice. A person who has attained the Way is also like this:
within the state of non-effort (*anābhoga*), they apply effort; all circumstances, whether contrary to their feelings or favorable, are embraced with a heart of compassion.
When one reaches this point, even the ancients would reprimand themselves, saying: "When there is complete clarity, there is nothing [to be grasped]."
It can be understood. Yet, even within the realm of the profoundest mystery, one must further apply critical scrutiny.

The five ranks of the Dongshan school—interchanging the direct and the indirect—are indeed extraordinary in their manner of engaging others. But when one reaches this supreme state, [the matter is different].

Only then can it be thus; there is no need for contrivance—it is naturally and perfectly so. Fushan Yuan took the public case where a monk asked Dongshan, "When cold and heat arrive, how does one avoid them?
and established it as the standard for the Five Ranks (*wuwei*). If you can understand this single case, [you will understand all].
The rest you may know for yourselves. Yantou said, "It is like a gourd on the water; as soon as it is pressed down, it turns over, requiring not even a hair’s breadth of effort.
Once, a monk asked Dongshan, "What is it like when Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra come to visit?"
Mount Shishuang said, "Go and join the herd of water buffaloes. A monk said, "Entering hell like an arrow, Master? Shishuang said, "It is entirely due to his power.
Dongshan said, "Why not go to where there is neither cold nor heat? This is "attaining the center within the partial.
The monk asked, "What is the place where there is neither cold nor heat? Dongshan said, "When it is cold, it freezes you to death; when it is hot..."
"Killing the teacher with heat—this is 'the partial within the central. Though it is central, it is partial; though it is partial, it is central.

Under Dongshan there are the stone woman, the wooden horse, the bottomless basket, the night-bright curtain, the dead snake, and so forth—the eighteen kinds—all of which clarify the central position."
Chan Master Wansong Xiu said: "Muzhou said, 'To tear it apart is up to me; to gather it together is up to me.
When asked about tearing it apart, he would immediately lift up a bundle of rope. When asked about gathering it together, he would simply sit with his hands folded.

Although he was thus free to withdraw or extend as he pleased, it was very much like being put to work by another. Dongshan criticized this, saying that the dialogue had been split into two separate pieces, resulting in a broken needle and severed thread."
I do not see the Way. To speak in such a manner is easy; to maintain continuity is extremely difficult. You must remain present while being perfectly extinguished;
be rolled up yet ever more expansive. Like interlocking hooks and rings, this is called the unbroken flow of the life-blood.
The school of Yaoshan is truly difficult to inherit and uphold. When Yunyan swept the floor, the dust rose to the heavens;
when Luopu took it to heart, he voiced his grievances without end. It is well that one who has no tongue can speak and one who has no hands can wield the staff;
yet, even if staff and shout are deployed in tandem, one only manages to grasp half of it from the side.
The Postscript:

Xinfeng established the Five Ranks (*wuwei*) to elucidate the principle of the "wondrous embrace within the central path. Although it consists of merely a few words, the methods for realizing the Way and the applications for guiding others are fully contained therein.
In realizing the Way, the stages of practice (*gong*) and the ranks of realization (*wei*) are mutually clarified; and...

Reaching the ultimate point where both function and status are simultaneously extinguished, when engaging with others, the roles of sovereign and minister are employed interchangeably until the ultimate harmony between sovereign and minister is attained.
For the most part, this involves pruning the dense forest of various views and cutting through the artificiality of myriad conceptualizations;

it must culminate in the state where idle names are exhausted and extinguished before it ceases. How could this be compared to the reckless Zen of those who are muddled and the pedantic learning of those who are narrow-minded?
How the ancestral hall has become muddled and confused! This Dharma should be spoken for those who understand its people; it should not be spoken for those who do not.
Because those who understand do not cling to verbal explanations, whether they speak of phenomena or principles, everything is realized as the ultimate realm.
Those who do not understand cling exclusively to verbal explanations; thus, even if their words are profoundly mysterious and repeatedly subtle, they all fall into the traps of the present age.
Therefore, Chengguan (Zhao) said: "In our school, we establish the five ranks as the fundamental principle.

Yet people often clarify them through phenomena and principle, reconcile them through stillness and illumination, perceive them through subject and object, or understand them through essence and function; they fall entirely into the realm of the present moment.
How can this be called the wondrous 'special transmission outside the teachings'? At the very threshold of birth and death, what is it that provides true power? It is not at all like this."
As for the timing: to speculate upon it would be incorrect. Considering this, how could one allow passersby outside the gate to peer into its inner workings?
Since ancient times, the various venerable masters have kept this deeply secret within their chambers, not daring to circulate it lightly.
It was only during the late Song dynasty that it first became manifest in the world; however, as it was not a true lineage transmission, each person followed their own subjective interpretation.

They speculate and conjecture, taking a deer and calling it a horse, or referring to the south as the north. They compete with one another to transmit these practices, even to the point of falsely composing various treatises to deceive later students.
These students, failing to reach true understanding, indulge in them without ceasing, claiming that through this they may grasp the Caodong (Dongshan) school.
They do not realize that this is just like a madman who clings to poison as his daily meal; it can not only fail to satisfy his hunger, but will surely bring about his ruin.
How thirsty [for truth] I am! Moreover, there is the tragedy of harming one’s life and extinguishing one’s nature—is this not foolish?
In the winter of the Guiwei year, I examined the remnants of the Caodong school’s tenets as transmitted at Shaolin; they were preposterous and extremely erroneous.
Consequently, I reflected that I wished to stop them but could not, and wished to correct them but found no way. Should I then simply allow these errors to be passed down indefinitely? If so—
How could my heart bear to remain at ease? I have therefore composed two fascicles titled *The Ancient Tracks of the Caves* (*Dongshang Gucheng*) to privately instruct students.
In the spring of the Jiashen year, the draft was completed, though it had not yet been revised. It is now the summer of the Wuzi year that I have taken up the previous draft once more.
I have revised this four times over. Alas! How could I have helped it? Long ago, a monk asked Da-hong En: "I do not ask about the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials;
what of the matter of the Five Ranks of Lord and臣 (Minister)? The Master said, "This is not your realm.

The monk said, "If that is so, then the stone man claps his hands and the wooden woman laughs aloud. The Master said, "Like one who divines with a ladle, listening for an empty sound while fast asleep."
He was full of delirious talk, saying, "If you had not come up here to pose this question, how could you have seen the pivot of Shaolin?
The Master said, "To let you go would be unacceptable," and immediately struck him. I say: only when you have realized the intent of Dahong can you read this book;
otherwise, you will be ensnared and bound to death within a thicket of entanglements. Do not take it amiss that this old monk is so fond of you.
